title: Permission scope
content_data: TikTok API for Business permissions consist of three levels: first level, second level, and third level. If an access token grants you a first-level permission, then you can access all the endpoints related to the second-level and third-level permissions under the first-level permission with the access token. You can find out the permission hierarchy by navigating to My Apps > App > App Detail > Authorization > Scope of permission on TikTok API For Business [portal](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/homepage). After you have obtained `scope`, which represents the permission scope of an access token, from the response of [/oauth2/access_token/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1738373164380162) or [/oauth/token/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1739965703387137), you can see the tables below to find out the permission that a scope ID (value of `scope`) corresponds to, and the corresponding endpoint. Note that "/" in the Corresponding endpoint columns of the tables below means that no API endpoint path is related to the permission at the current level. For instance, a scope ID that corresponds to a second-level permission may have corresponding endpoints at the third level but none at the second-level. ## First-level permission ``` xtable | Scope
